summary.partial: Some checks took too long, so these results are incomplete. Try again in a minute for the full picture.

spf.title: Have you listed who can send your email?
spf.pass: Yes. Your domain publishes a list of the services allowed to send email for you.
spf.warn: Partly. You have a list, but it could be tighter so receivers trust it more.
spf.fail: There's a problem with your list of allowed senders, so your genuine emails may land in spam.
spf.info: We couldn't check your list of allowed senders this time.

dmarc.title: Can someone fake emails from you?
dmarc.pass: It's hard. Your domain tells receivers to block or quarantine fake mail.
dmarc.warn: It's possible. Your protection against fake emails could be stronger.
dmarc.fail: Yes, at the moment. There's nothing telling receivers what to do with fake mail from your domain.
dmarc.info: We couldn't check your protection against fake emails this time.

dkim.title: Are your emails signed?
dkim.pass: Yes. Your emails carry a signature that proves they really came from you.
dkim.warn: We couldn't confirm your emails are signed. This is worth a closer look.
dkim.fail: We found a problem with your email signature, so receivers may not trust your mail.
dkim.info: We couldn't check your email signature this time.

mx.title: Can your domain receive email?
mx.pass: Yes. Your domain says where its email should be delivered.
mx.warn: Mostly, but something about where your email is delivered could be more reliable.
mx.fail: Not reliably. Other mail servers may not know where to deliver your email.
mx.info: We couldn't check where your email is delivered this time.

mta-sts.title: Is your email protected in transit?
mta-sts.pass: Yes. Your domain insists that email sent to you travels over a secure connection.
mta-sts.warn: Not fully. Adding protection here stops attackers downgrading the connection. Worth improving, not urgent.
mta-sts.fail: There's a problem with your in-transit protection that's worth fixing.
mta-sts.info: We couldn't check your in-transit protection this time.

tlsrpt.title: Will you hear about delivery problems?
tlsrpt.pass: Yes. Other mail servers can send you reports if they have trouble delivering to you securely.
tlsrpt.warn: Not yet. Turning on delivery reports helps you spot problems early. Nice to have, not urgent.
tlsrpt.fail: Your delivery reports are set up but have a problem.
tlsrpt.info: We couldn't check your delivery reports this time.

blacklist.title: Is your mail server on a spam blocklist?
blacklist.pass: No. We didn't find your mail server on the blocklists we checked.
blacklist.warn: Possibly. It's listed on a minor blocklist, which can affect a few receivers.
blacklist.fail: Yes. Some receivers may reject your mail until this is cleared.
blacklist.info: We couldn't get a clear answer this time. Try again later.

bimi.title: Can your logo appear next to your emails?
bimi.pass: Yes. Your domain is set up to show your logo in email apps that support it.
bimi.warn: You've started setting this up, but something isn't quite right yet.
bimi.fail: Your logo set-up has a problem, so it won't be shown.
bimi.info: Not set up. This is optional and only worth doing once everything else is in place.

dns.title: Is your domain's address book healthy?
dns.pass: Yes. The records that point people to your website and email are answering properly.
dns.warn: Mostly, but your domain's set-up could be more resilient.
dns.fail: There's a problem with your domain's records that could affect your website and email.
dns.info: We couldn't check your domain's records this time.

https.title: Does your website load securely?
https.pass: Yes. Your website loads over a secure connection.
https.warn: Mostly, but visitors might not always be sent to the secure version.
https.fail: No. Visitors may see a security warning when they open your website.
https.info: We couldn't reach your website to check this time.

smtp.title: Is your mail server set up securely?
smtp.pass: Yes. Your mail server answers properly and supports encrypted connections.
smtp.warn: Mostly, but something about your mail server's security could be better.
smtp.fail: There's a problem with your mail server's security that's worth fixing.
smtp.info: We couldn't test your mail server this time.

ptr.title: Does your mail server identify itself properly?
ptr.pass: Yes. Its address and name match both ways.
ptr.warn: Partly. Its name and address don't fully match.
ptr.fail: No. Your mail server's address has no proper name attached to it.

spf_pass_hardfail.title: Have you listed who can send your email?
spf_pass_hardfail.label: Good
spf_pass_hardfail.text: Yes, and you tell receivers to reject anything sent from elsewhere.
spf_pass_hardfail.why: This stops spammers sending mail that claims to be from you.
spf_pass_hardfail.fix: Nothing to do. Remember to update it if you add a new service that sends email for you.

spf_softfail_all.title: Have you listed who can send your email?
spf_softfail_all.label: Worth improving
spf_softfail_all.text: Yes, but mail from unlisted senders is only marked as suspicious, not rejected.
spf_softfail_all.why: That's a common, safe starting point, but it gives fakes a better chance of getting through.
spf_softfail_all.fix: Once you're sure every service that sends for you is listed, tighten it (~all to -all), or rely on a strict DMARC policy.

spf_missing.title: Have you listed who can send your email?
spf_missing.label: Needs fixing
spf_missing.text: Not yet. There's no list of who's allowed to send email as you.
spf_missing.why: Your genuine emails are more likely to land in spam, and anyone can pretend to be you.
spf_missing.fix: Add an SPF record listing your email provider and any other services that send email for you (newsletters, booking systems, invoices).

spf_multiple.title: Have you listed who can send your email?
spf_multiple.label: Needs fixing
spf_multiple.text: You have more than one sender list, which confuses receiving servers. They will treat it as broken.
spf_multiple.why: Broken SPF means your mail may be rejected or sent to spam.
spf_multiple.fix: Merge them into a single SPF record.

spf_too_many_lookups.title: Is your sender list too complicated?
spf_too_many_lookups.label: Needs fixing
spf_too_many_lookups.text: Your sender list points to so many other lists that receivers give up checking it (the limit is 10).
spf_too_many_lookups.why: Receivers treat it as an error, so your email may fail checks and land in spam.
spf_too_many_lookups.fix: Remove services you no longer use, or 'flatten' the record. This is a common fix and we can help.

spf_pass_all.title: Have you listed who can send your email?
spf_pass_all.label: Needs fixing
spf_pass_all.text: Your list currently says anyone can send as you, which defeats the point.
spf_pass_all.why: Anyone can send email that passes as you.
spf_pass_all.fix: Change the end of your SPF record from +all to -all (or ~all). This is a quick fix.

spf_neutral_all.title: Have you listed who can send your email?
spf_neutral_all.label: Worth improving
spf_neutral_all.text: You have a list, but it doesn't tell receivers what to do with mail from anyone else.
spf_neutral_all.why: Receivers get no guidance, so fakes are treated the same as your genuine mail.
spf_neutral_all.fix: End your SPF record with -all (or ~all while you're checking).

dmarc_policy_reject.title: Can someone fake emails from you?
dmarc_policy_reject.label: Good
dmarc_policy_reject.text: No. You tell receivers to reject fake emails claiming to be from you.
dmarc_policy_reject.why: This is the strongest protection against people impersonating you.
dmarc_policy_reject.fix: Nothing to do. Keep an eye on your reports.

dmarc_policy_quarantine.title: Can someone fake emails from you?
dmarc_policy_quarantine.label: Worth improving
dmarc_policy_quarantine.text: Mostly no. Fake emails claiming to be from you are sent to spam folders.
dmarc_policy_quarantine.why: Good protection, though fakes may still be seen in spam folders.
dmarc_policy_quarantine.fix: When your reports show only genuine mail passing, move to p=reject.

dmarc_policy_none.title: Can someone fake emails from you?
dmarc_policy_none.label: Needs fixing
dmarc_policy_none.text: Yes, at the moment. Your domain tells receivers to deliver fake mail anyway.
dmarc_policy_none.why: Scammers can send invoices or donation requests that look like they came from you.
dmarc_policy_none.fix: Move your DMARC policy to quarantine, then reject, once your genuine senders pass. This is usually a quick fix.

dmarc_missing.title: Can someone fake emails from you?
dmarc_missing.label: Needs fixing
dmarc_missing.text: Yes. Your domain has no DMARC policy, so receivers don't know what to do with fakes.
dmarc_missing.why: Gmail and Microsoft now expect DMARC from senders. Without it, your mail is more likely to be filtered, and impersonation is easy.
dmarc_missing.fix: Add a DMARC record, starting with monitoring and tightening it over a few weeks.

dmarc_no_rua.title: Do you get reports on who's sending as you?
dmarc_no_rua.label: Worth improving
dmarc_no_rua.text: No. Your DMARC policy doesn't ask for reports.
dmarc_no_rua.why: Reports show who is sending email using your name, both genuine services and fakes.
dmarc_no_rua.fix: Add a reporting address (rua=) to your DMARC record.

dmarc_invalid.title: Can someone fake emails from you?
dmarc_invalid.label: Needs fixing
dmarc_invalid.text: Your DMARC record has a mistake in it, so receivers may ignore it.
dmarc_invalid.why: A broken policy gives you no protection.
dmarc_invalid.fix: Fix the record so it includes a valid policy (p=none, quarantine or reject).

dkim_found.title: Are your emails signed?
dkim_found.label: Good
dkim_found.text: Yes. We found a signing key, so receivers can check your emails haven't been tampered with.
dkim_found.why: Signed mail is trusted more and is less likely to land in spam.

dkim_not_found_common_selectors.title: Are your emails signed?
dkim_not_found_common_selectors.label: Couldn't check
dkim_not_found_common_selectors.text: We couldn't find a signing key in the usual places. Your provider may use a custom one, so this isn't always a problem.
dkim_not_found_common_selectors.why: Unsigned mail is trusted less and more likely to land in spam.
dkim_not_found_common_selectors.fix: Check that DKIM signing is switched on with your email provider. Our full report looks more deeply.

mx_ok.title: Can your domain receive email?
mx_ok.label: Good
mx_ok.text: Yes. Your domain says which servers accept its email, and we could find them.
mx_ok.why: Without this, nobody can email you at your domain.

mx_missing.title: Can your domain receive email?
mx_missing.label: Needs fixing
mx_missing.text: We couldn't find any servers set up to receive email for your domain.
mx_missing.why: Emails sent to your addresses will bounce or vanish.
mx_missing.fix: Add MX records pointing to your email provider. Your provider's setup guide lists the exact values.

mx_unresolved.title: Can your domain receive email?
mx_unresolved.label: Worth improving
mx_unresolved.text: Your domain points to a mail server we couldn't find, so email to you may not arrive.
mx_unresolved.why: Senders can't deliver to a server that doesn't exist.
mx_unresolved.fix: Check the MX record's server name with your email provider.

mx_null.title: Can your domain receive email?
mx_null.label: Not used
mx_null.text: Your domain says it doesn't receive email. That's fine if it's deliberate.
mx_null.why: Anyone emailing this domain gets a bounce straight away.
mx_null.fix: Nothing to do if this domain isn't used for email.

mtasts_enforce.title: Is your email protected in transit?
mtasts_enforce.label: Good
mtasts_enforce.text: Yes. Other servers must use a secure, verified connection when sending you email.
mtasts_enforce.why: This stops attackers quietly intercepting email on its way to you.

mtasts_testing.title: Is your email protected in transit?
mtasts_testing.label: Optional
mtasts_testing.text: Partly. Your policy is in testing mode, so problems are reported but not blocked.
mtasts_testing.why: Testing is a sensible first step, but it doesn't yet protect your mail.
mtasts_testing.fix: After a few weeks of clean reports, switch the policy to enforce.

mtasts_missing.title: Is your email protected in transit?
mtasts_missing.label: Optional
mtasts_missing.text: Not fully. Without MTA-STS, an attacker could force email to you over an insecure connection.
mtasts_missing.why: It's a less common attack, but this closes it off.
mtasts_missing.fix: Publish an MTA-STS policy. It's worth improving, not urgent.

mtasts_policy_error.title: Is your email protected in transit?
mtasts_policy_error.label: Worth improving
mtasts_policy_error.text: You've started setting this up, but we couldn't read your policy file, so it isn't working yet.
mtasts_policy_error.why: Without a readable policy, other servers ignore it.
mtasts_policy_error.fix: Make sure https://mta-sts.yourdomain/.well-known/mta-sts.txt loads and lists a mode.

mtasts_none.title: Is your email protected in transit?
mtasts_none.label: Optional
mtasts_none.text: It's set up but switched off, so it isn't protecting anything yet.
mtasts_none.why: Testing, then enforcing, closes off attacks that downgrade the connection.
mtasts_none.fix: Switch the policy to testing, then enforce.

tlsrpt_ok.title: Will you hear about delivery problems?
tlsrpt_ok.label: Good
tlsrpt_ok.text: Yes. Other servers will report when they can't deliver to you securely.
tlsrpt_ok.why: You'll spot problems before they turn into missing email.

tlsrpt_missing.title: Will you hear about delivery problems?
tlsrpt_missing.label: Optional
tlsrpt_missing.text: No. You haven't asked other servers to report secure-delivery failures.
tlsrpt_missing.why: Problems could go unnoticed until someone says your email never arrived.
tlsrpt_missing.fix: Add a TLS reporting (TLSRPT) record. It takes one line of DNS.

blacklist_clean.title: Is your mail server on a spam blocklist?
blacklist_clean.label: Good
blacklist_clean.text: No. Your mail servers aren't on any of the blocklists we checked.
blacklist_clean.why: Listed servers have their email rejected or sent to spam.

blacklist_listed.title: Is your mail server on a spam blocklist?
blacklist_listed.label: Needs fixing
blacklist_listed.text: Yes. Some receivers may reject your email until this is cleared.
blacklist_listed.why: Your emails may be bouncing or going to spam without you knowing.
blacklist_listed.fix: Find and fix the cause (often a hacked account or a shared server), then request removal. We can help.

blacklist_inconclusive.title: Is your mail server on a spam blocklist?
blacklist_inconclusive.label: Couldn't check
blacklist_inconclusive.text: We couldn't get a clear answer this time. The full report uses a more reliable check.
blacklist_inconclusive.why: Listed servers have their email rejected or sent to spam.
blacklist_inconclusive.fix: Request the full report, or try again later.

blacklist_no_ips.title: Is your mail server on a spam blocklist?
blacklist_no_ips.label: Couldn't check
blacklist_no_ips.text: We couldn't find a mail server address to check, so we skipped this one.
blacklist_no_ips.why: Listed servers have their email rejected or sent to spam.
blacklist_no_ips.fix: Nothing to do unless this domain sends email.

bimi_ok.title: Does your logo show in inboxes?
bimi_ok.label: Good
bimi_ok.text: Yes. You've set up BIMI, so supporting inboxes can show your logo next to your emails.
bimi_ok.why: It's a small boost to trust and recognition.

bimi_missing.title: Does your logo show in inboxes?
bimi_missing.label: Optional
bimi_missing.text: Not yet. This is optional, and it only works once your DMARC policy is strict.
bimi_missing.why: Some inboxes show your logo next to your emails, which helps people trust them.
bimi_missing.fix: Optional. Consider it after DMARC is set to quarantine or reject.

dns_ok.title: Is your domain's DNS set up reliably?
dns_ok.label: Good
dns_ok.text: Yes. Your domain has more than one nameserver answering properly.
dns_ok.why: If your DNS goes down, so do your email and website.

dns_single_ns.title: Is your domain's DNS set up reliably?
dns_single_ns.label: Worth improving
dns_single_ns.text: Your domain relies on a single nameserver.
dns_single_ns.why: If it goes down, your email and website stop working.
dns_single_ns.fix: Use a DNS provider with at least two nameservers.

dns_no_nameservers.title: Is your domain's DNS set up reliably?
dns_no_nameservers.label: Needs fixing
dns_no_nameservers.text: We couldn't find the servers that answer for your domain.
dns_no_nameservers.why: Without them, your website and email stop working.
dns_no_nameservers.fix: Check the domain is registered and its nameservers are set at your registrar.

dns_ns_unresolved.title: Is your domain's DNS set up reliably?
dns_ns_unresolved.label: Worth improving
dns_ns_unresolved.text: One of the servers that answers for your domain can't be found.
dns_ns_unresolved.why: Some lookups will fail, making your website and email unreliable.
dns_ns_unresolved.fix: Remove or fix the broken nameserver at your registrar.

https_ok.title: Is your website secure?
https_ok.label: Good
https_ok.text: Yes. Your website loads over a secure connection.
https_ok.why: Browsers warn visitors away from insecure sites.

https_fail.title: Is your website secure?
https_fail.label: Needs fixing
https_fail.text: We couldn't load your website securely.
https_fail.why: Visitors may see a security warning or an error page.
https_fail.fix: Check your website's certificate and hosting. Many hosts offer free certificates.

https_http_error.title: Is your website secure?
https_http_error.label: Worth improving
https_http_error.text: Your website answered, but with an error, so visitors may not see your pages.
https_http_error.why: Visitors may think your site is down.
https_http_error.fix: Check your hosting or ask your web developer. It's fine if this domain is only used for email.

https_www_only.title: Is your website secure?
https_www_only.label: Worth improving
https_www_only.text: Only with www in front. Visitors who type your address without it may not reach your site.
https_www_only.why: Many people type the short version, and they'll see an error.
https_www_only.fix: Make the bare domain redirect to www. Most hosts and DNS providers have a setting for this.

smtp_ok.title: Is your mail server set up securely?
smtp_ok.label: Good
smtp_ok.text: Yes. Your mail server answers properly and supports encrypted connections.
smtp_ok.why: Email sent to you is protected on the way in.

smtp_starttls_missing.title: Does your mail server encrypt incoming email?
smtp_starttls_missing.label: Needs fixing
smtp_starttls_missing.text: No. Your mail server doesn't offer an encrypted connection.
smtp_starttls_missing.why: Email sent to you travels across the internet readable by anyone in the path.
smtp_starttls_missing.fix: Enable STARTTLS with a valid certificate on your mail server, or ask your provider.

smtp_unreachable.title: Is your mail server set up securely?
smtp_unreachable.label: Couldn't check
smtp_unreachable.text: We couldn't connect to your mail server from our test location this time.
smtp_unreachable.why: This doesn't always mean there's a problem, as some networks block test connections.
smtp_unreachable.fix: If people also report bounces, check your mail server is running and reachable.

cert_ok.title: Is your mail server's certificate valid?
cert_ok.label: Good
cert_ok.text: Yes. Its security certificate is valid and in date.
cert_ok.why: Valid certificates let other servers trust the connection.

cert_expiring_soon.title: Is your mail server's certificate valid?
cert_expiring_soon.label: Worth improving
cert_expiring_soon.text: It's valid, but it expires soon.
cert_expiring_soon.why: When it expires, some servers will stop delivering email to you securely, or at all.
cert_expiring_soon.fix: Renew it now, or set up automatic renewal.

cert_expired.title: Is your mail server's certificate valid?
cert_expired.label: Needs fixing
cert_expired.text: No. Your mail server's certificate has expired.
cert_expired.why: Servers with strict security, including yours if you use MTA-STS, may refuse to deliver email.
cert_expired.fix: Renew the certificate straight away and set up automatic renewal.

cert_invalid.title: Is your mail server's certificate valid?
cert_invalid.label: Needs fixing
cert_invalid.text: No. The certificate doesn't match your mail server's name, or isn't trusted.
cert_invalid.why: Other servers can't confirm they're talking to the real you.
cert_invalid.fix: Install a certificate issued for your mail server's hostname, from a trusted authority.

smtp_tls_failed.title: Does your mail server encrypt incoming email?
smtp_tls_failed.label: Worth improving
smtp_tls_failed.text: It offers encryption, but the secure connection failed when we tried it.
smtp_tls_failed.why: Senders may fall back to unencrypted delivery, or fail to deliver.
smtp_tls_failed.fix: Check the mail server's TLS settings and certificate, or ask your provider.

smtp_not_checked.title: Is your mail server set up securely?
smtp_not_checked.label: Couldn't check
smtp_not_checked.text: We couldn't test your mail server this time.
smtp_not_checked.why: This doesn't mean there's a problem.
smtp_not_checked.fix: Nothing to do. Ask us if you'd like it checked again.

ptr_ok.title: Does your mail server identify itself properly?
ptr_ok.label: Good
ptr_ok.text: Yes. Its address and name match both ways.
ptr_ok.why: Receivers trust servers whose name and address match.

ptr_missing.title: Does your mail server identify itself properly?
ptr_missing.label: Needs fixing
ptr_missing.text: No. Your mail server's address has no name attached to it.
ptr_missing.why: Many receivers reject or spam-filter mail from servers without a matching name.
ptr_missing.fix: Ask your hosting provider to set reverse DNS (PTR) for the server's IP address.

ptr_mismatch.title: Does your mail server identify itself properly?
ptr_mismatch.label: Worth improving
ptr_mismatch.text: Partly. Its address points to a name that doesn't point back to the same address.
ptr_mismatch.why: Some receivers treat this as suspicious.
ptr_mismatch.fix: Make the reverse DNS name and the server's own DNS record match.

ptr_not_checked.title: Does your mail server identify itself properly?
ptr_not_checked.label: Couldn't check
ptr_not_checked.why: This doesn't mean there's a problem.

check_error.text: We couldn't complete this check this time. Try again in a minute.
